svg.text: ux.md · vision.md · design.md ARE ALL INTERPRETATIONS OF RESEARCH
A pile of findings does not contain user needs. Findings record what happened. A need is a claim about what should be true for one product.
Somebody has to make that leap. The leap is where the product value is created, it is legitimately not evidence, and it has to be marked as a leap.
Each row below authors something new, rests it on evidence, and can never be graded above what it rests on. Blue = research owns · red = UX owns · amber = the leap.
findings.yaml
WHAT HAPPENED. Someone did a thing, or said a thing.
observed_behavior · stated_attitude — the only two rungs
that record reality rather than read it
Research authors AND grades. Nothing downstream may overwrite.
NOT TAILORED TO ANY PRODUCT
A finding is true about the people it was gathered from, on the
date it was gathered, about the build it was gathered against.
It is not about your feature. It cannot be, and asking it to be
is how scope gets widened.
THE LEAP — abduction. Owned by UX. Not a finding, not an unsupported guess. A third thing.
Her vocabulary already has the slots: claim_type: inferred · status: hypothesis · origin: design · invalidates_if · G17 caps it at LOW until research backs it.
Nothing REQUIRES them where the leap happens. That is the hole in both halves: hers stops overclaiming, mine stops dropping, neither marks the leap.
ux.md — authors THE NEED
"Given this evidence, here is the problem, and whose it is."
scope: mostly existence / pattern — claims about what IS
typical rung: inferred, resting on observed + stated findings
✓ has ## Evidence · ceiling check runs
THE NEED IS NEW CONTENT, NOT A RESTATEMENT
This is the file where a need statement first exists. It is not in
findings.yaml and could not be — findings are about what happened,
needs are about what should be true. So this claim is authored, and
it still cannot be graded above the findings under it.
Limitation: rests_on: takes ONE finding. A need usually rests on several.
vision.md — authors THE BET
"Given this evidence, here is what would be valuable."
scope: ADOPTION — will they want it, keep it, pay for it
status: hypothesis · origin: design / product_brief
G17: cannot be High until research backs it · G18: usability
evidence cannot answer this question at all
THE HIGHEST-RISK FILE, AND IT HAD NO CHECK UNTIL TODAY
A vision is an adoption claim by construction. Adoption evidence is the
thing we have least of — in this corpus, none. So the file making the
least checkable claims was the one nothing looked at, while ux.md,
whose claims are mostly about what already happens, carried the only check.
This is why [SCOPE: adoption] is the tag to KEEP, not trade away.
Reversing what I said yesterday — vision is exactly what it is for.
design.md — authors THE BEHAVIOUR
"Given this evidence, here is how it must behave."
scope: usability — can they do it, did they do it unaided
the one file with claims that rest on STANDARDS, not findings:
WCAG, APEX, the FLOOR items. Those need no evidence row.
USABILITY EVIDENCE LIVES HERE AND ONLY ANSWERS HERE
"9 of 12 completed unaided" belongs to this file. It says nothing about
whether anyone will adopt the thing — that is the row above, and the
G18 failure is answering a vision question with a design finding.
FLOOR items are the only claims in the system that are legitimately unsourced.
Intent Spec §5 → the build
THE COMMITMENT. UXI-## · append-only · inherits forward.
This is where code spec-driven design starts. Everything above it
is the part code SDD assumes someone else got right.
A ROW CAN OUTLIVE ITS BASIS
The id survives a re-grade; the justification quietly does not. Nothing
re-opens a UXI row when research lowers the finding under it. That is the
missing half of "it is a loop, not a snapshot."
